summary: Defines a new BGP extended community type that carries a 4-octet AS number.

eli5.summary: Networks have ID numbers that have grown large. This adds a tag in BGP that can hold the bigger number.

questions: what is a 4-octet as extended community
what is bgp route target type 0x0202
subtitle: A BGP extended community that can carry a 4-octet AS number, with two route-target and route-origin types.

tldr.problem: BGP extended communities could name an Autonomous System only with a 2-octet number, which cannot hold a 4-octet AS number.
tldr.mechanism: A new extended community type has a 4-octet Global Administrator field holding the AS number and a 2-octet Local Administrator field the AS owner can use as it likes.
tldr.outcome: IANA assigned 0x0202 for a route target and 0x0203 for a route origin, and 2-octet ASes SHOULD keep using the 2-octet communities.

today: RFC 5668 is a Proposed Standard, and no later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: This document defines a new type of BGP extended community (RFC 4360): the 4-octet AS specific extended community. It is similar to the 2-octet AS specific extended community, except that it can carry a 4-octet Autonomous System number.
sections.eli5: It is the same kind of tag as before, only with room for a longer network number.

sections.title: Format of the Community
sections.content:
This is an extended type with a Type field of 2 octets and a Value field of 6 octets. The high-order octet of the type is 0x02 for transitive communities or 0x42 for non-transitive ones. The low-order octet is the sub-type.

The Value field has two sub-fields: a 4-octet Global Administrator holding an AS number assigned by IANA, and a 2-octet Local Administrator in which the organization identified by that AS can encode any information. Its format and meaning should be defined by the sub-type.
sections.eli5: The tag has a part for the network's number and a part the network can fill in however it wants.

sections.title: Two-Octet Autonomous Systems
sections.content:
Under RFC 4893, a 2-octet AS number becomes a 4-octet one by setting the 2 high-order octets to zero. So an AS with a 2-octet number could in principle use either kind of community, but the two would be treated as different even with the same sub-type and Local Administrator values.

For backward compatibility and to avoid inconsistencies, ASes that use 2-octet AS numbers SHOULD use 2-octet AS specific extended communities rather than 4-octet ones.
sections.eli5: If your network number is still short, keep using the short tag so nobody gets confused.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
IANA created and maintains a registry called Four-octet AS Specific Extended Community. Future assignments use First Come First Served. Transitive types are 0x0200 to 0x02ff and non-transitive types are 0x4200 to 0x42ff.

This document assigns 0x0202 to the four-octet AS specific Route Target and 0x0203 to the Route Origin. It adds no new security issues; the considerations for BGP extended communities apply, and it points to separate work on handling malformed optional transitive attributes.
sections.eli5: An official list says which tag numbers mean what, and this RFC claims two of them.

fields.name: Local Administrator
fields.desc: Any information the AS owner chooses.
